sentences.en: And you're, you're, you're coming up on 30, you're in your late 20s, end of your 30s.
sentences.zh: 而且你，你，你快30岁了，你二十多岁快三十，三十岁末。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, you're looking ahead and you're thinking about children and the future.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，你向前看，开始考虑孩子和未来。

sentences.en: And I really, I bought Marshall's kind of slide into the seduction.
sentences.zh: 而我真的，我挺能理解马歇尔那种一步步陷入诱惑的过程。

sentences.en: Obviously, it's funny and it's silly and we maybe tried to make it amusing, but I think it's pretty real, right?
sentences.zh: 显然，这很有趣也很傻，我们可能试图把它搞得引人发笑，但我认为它相当真实，对吧？

sentences.en: That even a guy with all of those kind of values who is a cuddly, sweet, empathetic bear of a guy, there is something seductive when someone whispers in your ear and goes, like,
sentences.zh: 甚至连一个有着所有那种价值观、像个可爱、温柔、富有同理心的熊一样的家伙，当有人在你耳边低语时，也会有一种诱惑，就像是，

sentences.en: deep down your wife wants you to be rich.
sentences.zh: 内心深处你妻子希望你成为富翁。

sentences.en: Your wife wants everything.
sentences.zh: 你妻子什么都想要。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But, but not only that, there's a gravitational pull to a culture, you know?
sentences.zh: 但是，不仅如此，对一种文化有一种引力，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I, I know a woman who moved down to Florida kind of mid-pandemic with her husband and her kids, and she was very kind of New York progressive.
sentences.zh: 我，我认识一个女人，在疫情中期和她丈夫以及孩子搬到了佛罗里达，她很大程度上是那种纽约的进步派。

sentences.en: Her politics were just like line drive kind of New York City politics.
sentences.zh: 她的政治立场简直就是那种根正苗红的纽约市政治。

sentences.en: And she moved down to Florida, and she was surrounded by different political beliefs.
sentences.zh: 然后她搬到了佛罗里达，身边都是不同的政治信仰。

sentences.en: And she said, like, I still consider myself on the left end of the spectrum, but it changed a lot of my thinking.
sentences.zh: 她说，我仍然认为自己属于光谱的左翼，但这改变了我的很多想法。

sentences.en: Just being saturated in a different culture.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是浸润在不同的文化中。

sentences.en: So Marshall, like, steps into this culture and it rattles him because he also doesn't want to get made fun of at lunch.
sentences.zh: 所以马歇尔，踏入了这种文化，这让他感到不安，因为他也不想在午餐时被嘲笑。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to eat alone.
sentences.zh: 他不想一个人吃饭。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to feel like he's the lame kid, right?
sentences.zh: 他不想觉得自己是个逊咖，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, and it's funny how adolescent fear of being left out never quite leaves us, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，说来有趣，那种害怕被排挤的青春期恐惧从未真正离开我们，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, it's always, it's always a driver.
sentences.zh: 就像，它总是，它总是一个驱动力。

sentences.en: And that's also primal, like, shame of being, you know, cast out of the tribe, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是那种原始的，被排挤出部落的羞耻感，对吧？

sentences.en: I remember being in my 20s, writing for Late Show with David Letterman, growing up all of my teen years, hating how much my father smoked cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 我记得二十多岁时，在《大卫·莱特曼深夜秀》担任编剧，我整个青少年时期都在讨厌我父亲抽烟抽得那么厉害。

sentences.en: We would go on long car trips, and he'd be smoking with the air conditioner with, like, me and, like, a friend of mine and my mother driving on, like,
sentences.zh: 我们会进行长途汽车旅行，他一边开着空调抽烟，车里有我、还有我的一个朋友以及我母亲，开着车去，就像，

sentences.en: a long car trip to go away for the weekend.
sentences.zh: 去过周末的长途汽车旅行。

sentences.en: And, like, the whole car was smoking the cigarette.
sentences.zh: 然后，整辆车都在抽烟。

sentences.en: Like, every, the car itself was smoking the cigarette.
sentences.zh: 就像，每个人，车本身都在抽烟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I was like, the one thing I know about myself, you know, life may come at me in all kinds of directions, but the one thing I know is I'm never going to smoke.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，我对自己最清楚的一点是，你知道，生活可能会从各个方向向我袭来，但我知道的一点是我绝不会抽烟。

sentences.en: Except when you're drunk.
sentences.zh: 除非你喝醉了。

sentences.en: Except when I'm drunk, yes.
sentences.zh: 除非我喝醉了，是的。

sentences.en: Well, very much to the point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，非常切中要害。

sentences.en: But I remember being at Letterman, and I don't want to name names, Carter Bays was a big smoker, and a couple of the other writers at Letterman.
sentences.zh: 但我记得在莱特曼节目组的时候，我不想指名道姓，卡特·贝斯是个老烟枪，莱特曼组里还有其他几个编剧。

sentences.en: And, by the way, much to his credit, Carter quit smoking years and years and years and years ago.
sentences.zh: 而且，顺便说一句，值得称赞的是，卡特在好多年好多年以前就把烟戒了。

sentences.en: In fact, it was led to material.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这还被写成了素材。

sentences.en: There was a whole Hymium episode about that last cigarette ever.
sentences.zh: 《老爸老妈浪漫史》里甚至有一整集就是关于最后一根烟的。

sentences.en: And I, somewhere in my, like, early-mid-20s, because of Carter and a couple of the other dudes at, the other writers at Letterman smoked, I started sort of smoking, like,
sentences.zh: 而我，在二十岁出头到中期的某个时候，因为卡特和莱特曼的其他几个伙计、其他编剧抽烟，我也开始抽起烟来，就像，

sentences.en: not even enjoying it.
sentences.zh: 甚至并不享受。

sentences.en: I didn't look cool doing it.
sentences.zh: 我抽烟的时候看起来一点也不酷。

sentences.en: I'm the one person that, while smoking, looks really uncool and kind of sickly.
sentences.zh: 我是那种一边抽烟，一边看起来极其不酷还带点病态的人。

sentences.en: Like, I just sort of turned a bad color.
sentences.zh: 就像，我的脸色会变得很难看。

sentences.en: It does not look like James Dean at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不像詹姆斯·迪恩。

sentences.en: And I was thinking, like, why am I doing this?
sentences.zh: 然后我在想，我为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: I hate this.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌这样。

sentences.en: I actually hate this.
sentences.zh: 我其实讨厌这样。

sentences.en: And our office became the smoking office, because I had, like, windows that opened.
sentences.zh: 然后我们的办公室就成了吸烟办公室，因为我的窗户是可以打开的。

sentences.en: It was, like, over the Ed Sullivan Theater, and, you know, where Colbert is now.
sentences.zh: 那个位置大概在埃德·沙利文剧场上方，也就是科尔伯特现在所在的那个地方。

sentences.en: And we were supposed to, people would come in there to smoke.
sentences.zh: 当时我们那儿本来是规定，人们会去那里抽烟。

sentences.en: So the fucking whole office became, like, an ashtray.
sentences.zh: 所以他妈的整个办公室简直就成了一个大烟灰缸。

sentences.en: And it was so disgusting.
sentences.zh: 而且真的太恶心了。

sentences.en: And eventually, I had, like, a moment where I was like, I was never going to do this.
sentences.zh: 到最后，我经历了一个瞬间，当时我就觉得，我绝不能这样下去。

sentences.en: And I think I'm doing this to fit in with, I basically did, like, the high school thing, but in my 20s.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我这么做是为了融入大家，我基本上是在二十多岁的时候，过了一把高中生活的那种瘾。

sentences.en: I never did the high school thing in high school.
sentences.zh: 我上高中的时候可没经历过什么高中生活。

sentences.en: I never had that peer pressure in my 20s.
sentences.zh: 我在二十多岁时从来没有承受过那种同辈压力。

sentences.en: I was like, I would smoke.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，我会抽烟的。

sentences.en: And it wasn't a huge amount, but it was somewhat.
sentences.zh: 虽然量不是很大，但确实抽一些。

sentences.en: And I remember just looking at myself in the mirror at some point and going, like, this is who you were never going to be.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次我照着镜子看着自己，心里想，这根本不是你原本发誓绝不想成为的那种人吗。

sentences.en: And you're doing it to fit in with these dudes.
sentences.zh: 而你现在却在为了融入这群家伙而这么做。

sentences.en: Well, it's also, it's so easy to moralize.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这也是，道德说教实在是太容易了。

sentences.en: I remember being, having a conversation with my friend Jeremy Hirshfield in eighth grade.
sentences.zh: 我记得在八年级的时候，我和朋友杰里米·赫什菲尔德有过一次对话。

sentences.en: We were at this private school.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在那所私立学校里。

sentences.en: We were both about to go into this public school.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都快要转到一所公立学校去了。

sentences.en: And he said, I might try alcohol.
sentences.zh: 他说，我可能会尝试一下酒精。

sentences.en: And I said, I remember I was so self-righteous.
sentences.zh: 我当时回答说，我记得自己当时是那么的自以为是。

sentences.en: I was like, I don't need to have alcohol to have a good time, is what I said.
sentences.zh: 我当时说的是，我不需要靠酒精来获得快乐。

sentences.en: Cut to, like, two months into freshman year, I'm shotgunning beers in C.H.
sentences.zh: 镜头一转，大概到了高一开学两个月后，我正在C.H.

sentences.en: Waterman's attic.
sentences.zh: 沃特曼的阁楼里用漏斗狂灌啤酒。

sentences.en: You know, just, like, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，简直就是，完全如此。

sentences.en: I have no memory of saying that.
sentences.zh: 我完全不记得自己说过那种话了。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I mean, culture and that peer pressure, like, it's a huge driver.
sentences.zh: 但是，好吧，我是说，文化和同辈压力，这真的是一个巨大的驱动力。

sentences.en: I also think there's something really funny about the corporate critique that you guys laced into How I Met Your Mother with Goliath National Bank and whatever this company is that got acquired,
sentences.zh: 我也觉得，你们在《老爸老妈浪漫史》里融入的对企业文化的讽刺非常有意思，比如歌利亚国家银行，以及无论这是哪个被收购的公司，

sentences.en: perhaps, by Goliath National Bank.
sentences.zh: 说不定就是被歌利亚国家银行收购的。

sentences.en: And that they were very generically, besides the yellow fuzzy stuff on tennis balls, just involved.
sentences.zh: 除了网球上那种黄色的绒毛之外，它们非常泛泛地、切实地参与其中。

sentences.en: They had their hands in all evil, all global evil.
sentences.zh: 它们把手伸向了所有的邪恶，所有的全球邪恶。

sentences.en: They had their fingerprints on every aspect.
sentences.zh: 它们的指纹留在了每一个角落。

sentences.en: It's weapons.
sentences.zh: 涉及武器。

sentences.en: It's, like, everything.
sentences.zh: 简直是无所不包。

sentences.en: And, but it's funny how you did that within, like, a real corporate structure.
sentences.zh: 而且有意思的是，你们竟然是在一个真正的企业架构里做到这一点的。

sentences.en: Like, we were not in indie, like, outside.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们并不是身处独立公司，在圈子外面。

sentences.en: This is not like a John Waters film.
sentences.zh: 这可不是约翰·沃特斯的电影。

sentences.en: Like, this is, like, 20th century Fox, which at the time was owned by Rupert Murdoch, it must be said.
sentences.zh: 这就是二十世纪福斯公司，必须得说，当时它属于鲁珀特·默多克。

sentences.en: And you guys were doing this critique, which I thought was, like, pretty cool and subversive to be doing that from within.
sentences.zh: 而你们居然在进行这种批判，我觉得这在体制内部去搞这种反叛，实在是太酷了。

sentences.en: Yeah, you would throw to commercial from How I Met Your Mother and see ads for companies like AltruCell, essentially.
sentences.zh: 对啊，你从《老爸老妈浪漫史》切到广告时，看到的正是诸如阿尔特鲁细胞公司之类的广告。

sentences.en: Like, right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Like, those were our sponsors.
sentences.zh: 没错，那些就是我们的赞助商。

sentences.en: So there was, like, this was us hating ourselves a little bit, maybe, for making, for knowing we were some part of that corporate engine.
sentences.zh: 所以这就有点像，我们在制作时明知自己是那个企业机器的一部分，从而多少有点自我厌恶。

sentences.en: I remember going to work so many days and seeing that the giant Simpsons, you know, they're, like, when you drive into the Fox lot, there's,
sentences.zh: 我记得有很多天我去上班时，看到巨大的辛普森一家，你知道的，就当你把车开进福斯片场时，

sentences.en: on one of the side of one of the sound stages, there's a huge painting of the Simpsons.
sentences.zh: 在其中一个摄影棚的侧墙上，画着一幅巨大的辛普森一家的壁画。

sentences.en: Like, I hate 50 foot tall, you know, and Star Wars, and just going, like, okay, remember that stuff.
sentences.zh: 足足有50英尺高，还有《星球大战》，然后心里就会想，好吧，记住这些东西。

sentences.en: Because I know the larger parent company here has some real problems happening.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道这里的母公司正在发生一些真正的问题。

sentences.en: And I don't, I much like, I much prefer to think of ourselves as we are creative types working for this one completely separate faction, like the Simpsons,
sentences.zh: 我更愿意把自己想象成是一群富有创意的家伙，为这个完全独立的派系工作，就像《辛普森一家》那样，

sentences.en: which also is an unbelievable social satirical critique, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是一种令人难以置信的社会讽刺批判，对吧？

sentences.en: And I would have to really meditate some days on that type of, I'm thinking about it that way, as opposed to some other way.
sentences.zh: 有些日子我真的必须对着那种想法进行冥想，我是从那个角度去思考的，而不是从别的什么角度。

sentences.en: But we had to sneak in that commentary ourselves.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须自己悄悄把那种评论塞进去。

sentences.en: Don't you think, though, that we are from, like, we're kind of, like, late Gen X, you and I?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗，其实我们俩，我们差不多是属于较晚的一代X世代吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, we're from a generation that was, like, reality bites.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们这一代人，可以说是经历了《现实的创伤》那种心态。

sentences.en: Like, she chooses Ethan Hawke over Ben Stiller.
sentences.zh: 就像，她选择了伊桑·霍克而不是本·斯蒂勒。

sentences.en: Like, it's, it's, it's about not selling out.
sentences.zh: 就像，这，这，这就是关于不要向现实妥协、保持本色。

sentences.en: Spoilers.
sentences.zh: 剧透。

sentences.en: Yeah, sorry about that.
sentences.zh: 对，真是不好意思。

sentences.en: Like, what's Nate Bragazzi's thing about Sixth Sense?
sentences.zh: 内特·布拉加齐关于《第六感》是怎么想的？

sentences.en: Like, don't, oh, we're going to rent it tonight.
sentences.zh: 就像，别，哦，我们今晚正打算租来看呢。

sentences.en: Why would you ruin it?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要剧透？

sentences.en: But, but, um, I think that we, I, I know, I still have that kind of, like, don't sell out thing in me.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是，嗯，我觉得我们，我，我知道，我内心深处依然保留着那种，绝不向现实低头的劲头。

sentences.en: That, that's just generational.
sentences.zh: 那，那纯粹是属于我们这一代的烙印。

sentences.en: But at the same time, I don't think Gen Z, they do not have that.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我觉得 Z 世代，他们就没有那种概念。

sentences.en: Like, they will accept ads on their TikTok if they are killing it.
sentences.zh: 比如，只要能赚得盆满钵满，他们完全能接受在自己的 TikTok 里植入广告。

sentences.en: Like, I just think that the idea of being a sellout is not a thing anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以，我只是觉得“出卖灵魂”或者“向商业妥协”这种概念已经不复存在了。

sentences.en: That's why, um, a friend of mine, Isaac Butler, a really smart writer, he, we went and saw, uh,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，嗯，我的一个朋友艾萨克·巴特勒，一个非常聪明的作家，他，我们去看了，呃，

sentences.en: Merrily, we were all along with Daniel Radcliffe when it was at New York Theatre Workshop.
sentences.zh: 《欢乐我们远去》，当它还在纽约戏剧工场上演时，我们一直陪伴着丹尼尔·雷德克里夫。

sentences.en: And it's a, it's an amazing, if incredibly flawed musical.
sentences.zh: 这是一部，虽然有着极其明显的瑕疵，但依然非常精彩的音乐剧。

sentences.en: And he said, I think the reason this musical doesn't work, like, at its base level is it took place in the 70s or early 80s.
sentences.zh: 他说，我认为这部音乐剧行不通的原因，从根本上讲，是因为它的背景设定在 70 年代或 80 年代初。

sentences.en: And it all hinges on this notion of selling out.
sentences.zh: 而它的一切冲突都建立在“向现实妥协”这个概念上。

sentences.en: And that's just, it's not a thing anymore.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这已经根本不算个事儿了。

sentences.en: Like, no one gets mad at you for taking money from a big studio or a corporation to finance your dream project.
sentences.zh: 比如说，没有人会因为你拿了大制片厂或大公司的钱来资助你的梦想项目而生你的气。

sentences.en: Like, I just think we're in a different zone.
sentences.zh: 我就觉得我们现在处在完全不同的时代。

sentences.en: But I think you guys, we come from a kind of generation where there was a little bit of, like, ugh, or should we be doing this?
sentences.zh: 但我认为你们，我们来自这样一个世代：多少会有点那种，呃，或者说我们在做这个合适吗的纠结？

sentences.en: That's really interesting to think about.
sentences.zh: 这真的很值得思考。

sentences.en: I wonder how that, how this episode plays in that context in 2025.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道在 2025 年的语境下，这一集会是怎样一种呈现效果。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it plays just because it's really, it's less about, it's in part about selling out, but it's also, like, selling out to this incredibly evil company that is, like,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得它依然成立，因为这其实不完全是，其中一部分虽然关于妥协，但它同时也是，向这种极其邪恶的公司妥协，就是那种，

sentences.en: poisoning, clearly poisoning the environment.
sentences.zh: 污染，明显在污染环境的公司。

sentences.en: The background noise is the company.
sentences.zh: 背景噪音就是那家公司。

sentences.en: But the more pressing thing is these guys and the way they talk and the way they talk about women and the way they,
sentences.zh: 但更迫切的问题是这帮家伙以及他们说话的方式，他们谈论女性的方式，以及他们，

sentences.en: just their whole ethos of how they interact and how they move through that space.
sentences.zh: 也就是他们彼此互动以及在该空间中行事方式的整个核心调性。

sentences.en: And Marshall's like, this is, I have to learn a new language.
sentences.zh: 马歇尔就像是，天哪，我得学一门新语言。

sentences.en: Like, he has to code switch, essentially.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他必须得切换话语风格。
